\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Ornstein Uhlenbeck}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.OrnsteinUhlenbeck
\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.OrnsteinUhlenbeck}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Gaussian generator pair]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasGaussianGenerator}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasGaussianGenerator}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f,g:\bbr^n\to\bbr$. The pair $(f,g)$ has the
Gaussian generator property when both functions belong to $L^2$ for the $n$-dimensional
product standard Gaussian measure and, as $t\to0$ through positive values, the $L^2$
norm of $\bigl(f-P_{e^{-t}}f\bigr)/t-g$ tends to zero, where $P_{e^{-t}}f$ denotes
Gaussian noise with parameter $e^{-t}$ applied to $f$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Domain of the Gaussian generator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.InGaussianGeneratorDomain}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.InGaussianGeneratorDomain}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasGaussianGenerator}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\bbr^n\to\bbr$. Then $f$ lies in the Gaussian
generator domain exactly when there exists a function $g:\bbr^n\to\bbr$ such that both
$f$ and $g$ are square-integrable for product standard Gaussian measure and
$\bigl(f-P_{e^{-t}}f\bigr)/t$ converges to $g$ in that $L^2$ norm as $t\to0^+$, where
$P_{e^{-t}}$ is Gaussian noise with parameter $e^{-t}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Gaussian Ornstein–Uhlenbeck differential]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianOUDifferential}
\statementsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p008-b001}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{
  pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p011-b001,
  pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p012-b008
}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianOUDifferential}
\leanok
For a natural number $n$, a function $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and a point
$x\in\mathbb{R}^n$, define its Gaussian Ornstein–Uhlenbeck differential at $x$ by
$Df(x)[x]-\sum_{i=1}^n D\bigl(y\mapsto Df(y)[e_i]\bigr)(x)[e_i]$, where $e_i$ is the
$i$th coordinate vector and derivatives are understood as Fréchet derivatives.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Gaussian entropy functional]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianEntropy}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianEntropy}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
For a natural number $n$ and a real-valued function $f$ on $\bbr^n$, define its Gaussian
entropy by $\int f\log f\,d\gamma_n-\bigl(\int f\,d\gamma_n\bigr)\log\bigl(\int
f\,d\gamma_n\bigr)$, where $\gamma_n$ is product standard Gaussian measure on $\bbr^n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Uniqueness of the Gaussian generator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGenerator_unique}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGenerator_unique}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasGaussianGenerator}
Let $n\ge0$ and let $f,g,h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$. If both $g$ and $h$ are Gaussian
generators of $f$, then $g=h$ almost everywhere with respect to the product standard
Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$.
\end{theorem}

  {BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianOUDifferential}
  {context}
  {boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}
  {pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p008-b001}
Let $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be such that $f$ has Gaussian generator $g$, and
suppose that $f$ is three times continuously differentiable. Then $g$ agrees almost
everywhere, with respect to the product standard Gaussian measure, with the
Ornstein–Uhlenbeck differential of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Gaussian generator under noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGenerator_noise}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGenerator_noise}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasGaussianGenerator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise}
Let $n\ge0$, let $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, and suppose $g$ is the Gaussian
generator of $f$. For every $\rho\in[-1,1]$, the Gaussian noise averages of $f$ and $g$
with parameter $\rho$ have the same generator relation: the noise average of $g$ is a
Gaussian generator of the noise average of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Derivative of Gaussian noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_gaussianNoise}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_gaussianNoise}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasGaussianGenerator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, and suppose that both
are square-integrable for standard Gaussian product measure and that the positive-time
Gaussian noise difference quotients of $f$ converge to $g$ in $L^2$ as time tends to
zero. For any $\rho\in(-1,1)$ with $\rho\ne0$ and any $x\in\mathbb R^n$, the Gaussian
noise average of $f$ as a function of its correlation parameter is differentiable at
$\rho$, with derivative equal to the Gaussian noise average of $g$ at $\rho$, divided by
$\rho$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Derivative of Gaussian noise along the exponential parameter]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_gaussianNoise_exp}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_gaussianNoise_exp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasGaussianGenerator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be
square-integrable with respect to the product standard Gaussian measure. Suppose that,
as $u\to0^+$, the $L^2$ norm of $x\mapsto (f(x)-T_{e^{-u}}f(x))/u-g(x)$ tends to zero,
where $T_\rho f(x)$ is the Gaussian average of $f(\rho x+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,Y)$ for a
standard Gaussian vector $Y$. For every $t>0$ and $x\in\mathbb R^n$, the function
$s\mapsto T_{e^{-s}}f(x)$ is differentiable at $t$, with derivative $-T_{e^{-t}}g(x)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Self-adjointness of the Gaussian generator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGenerator_selfAdjoint}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGenerator_selfAdjoint}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasGaussianGenerator}
Let $n\ge0$ and let $f,g,u,v:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$. Suppose $u$ is the Gaussian
generator of $f$ and $v$ is the Gaussian generator of $g$. Then $\int f
v\,d\gamma_n=\int u g\,d\gamma_n$, where $\gamma_n$ is the product standard Gaussian
measure on $\mathbb R^n$.
\end{theorem}

\proofstep
  {BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasGaussianGenerator}
  {context}
  {mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}
  {pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p010-b007,
    pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p011-b001}
Let $n\ge0$ and let $\gamma_n$ be the product of $n$ standard Gaussian measures on
$\mathbb R^n$. Suppose $f,g,u,v:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ are such that $u$ is the
Gaussian generator of $f$ and $v$ is the Gaussian generator of $g$, and suppose $f$ and
$g$ are three times continuously differentiable. Then the function $x\mapsto\sum_{i=1}^n
\partial_i f(x)\,\partial_i g(x)$ is integrable with respect to $\gamma_n$, and $\int f
v\,d\gamma_n=\int\sum_{i=1}^n\partial_i f\,\partial_i g\,d\gamma_n$.
\end{theorem}

\proofstep
  {BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianEntropy}
  {direct}
  {boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}
  {pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p008-b001}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ belong to
Gaussian $L^2$. For $t>0$, define the Gaussian noise average $T_t f(x)=\int
f(e^{-t}x+\sqrt{1-e^{-2t}}y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$. Suppose that $(f-T_t f)/t$ converges to $g$
in Gaussian $L^2$ as $t\to0^+$. Then $f^2\log(f^2)$ is Gaussian integrable, and, writing
$\operatorname{Ent}_{\gamma_n}(h)=\int h\log h\,d\gamma_n-(\int h\,d\gamma_n)\log(\int
h\,d\gamma_n)$, one has
\[
\operatorname{Ent}_{\gamma_n}(f^2)\le 2\int fg\,d\gamma_n.
\]
\end{theorem}

  {BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianEntropy}
  {direct}
  {boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}
  {pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p008-b001}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, and suppose that $g$ is
the Gaussian generator of $f$ in the sense that both functions are square-integrable for
standard Gaussian product measure and the corresponding Gaussian noise difference
quotients converge to $g$ in $L^2$ as the positive time parameter tends to zero. If $f$
is three times continuously differentiable, then
\[
\operatorname{Ent}_\gamma(f^2)\le 2\int_{\mathbb
R^n}\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl(Df(x)[e_i]\bigr)^2\,d\gamma(x),
\]
where $\gamma$ is standard Gaussian product measure and $e_i$ is the $i$th coordinate
vector.
\end{theorem}
